questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The fact that I knew the French language had a big impact in my choice of going to France.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university seemed very used to having Erasmus students. There were organised a lot of social activities as well. The communication from the host university could have been better before the start of the semester.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We had a coordinator who met us the first day with a tour and an introduction.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I can't think of anything that would have improved it.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: A 10m2 room in a dormitory with a shared kitchen.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There was a shared kitchen with a kitchen stove and a microwave. Each room was equipped with its own fridge and refrigerator. You could buy cheap lunch at the university during the week days. For dinner on the week days, you could buy food from the cafeteria of the dormitory.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
The on campus housing is located around 15 minutes from the university campus (by foot).
The kitchen's are not the best, and there are no ovens.
The room's are also quite small, however I didn't need more space.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of steps and I was never sure whether I had completed everything or not.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Unfortunately, I don't remember.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: My coordinator from the host university sent guides for the different steps and was very accommodating.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately, I didn't get all the classes that I had hoped for, due to scheduling issues.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The exams were different for the Erasmus students.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The MA courses were naturally harder than the BA courses, however they were all manageable.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We only had oral exams. As Erasmus students we weren't given a case, but rather, we had to learn the whole course by heart. On top of that, we had no books and nothing to prepare for each lesson. The teacher's rarely had powerpoints or similar. Rather you had to rely on the notes you took during class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Institution et vie politique du Veme Republique, Droit de l'environnement, Droit de propriété littéraire et artistique, droit internationales économiques, droit des organisations internationales.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Droit de l'environnement, Droit de propriété littéraire et artistique.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You could apply for two sport activities per week for free.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Sporting activities, ESN (organisation that organises social events for Erasmus students) and more.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join as many ESN activities as possible.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the area. There are some amazing hikes!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open from the start.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How everything was more relaxed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get notes from French students for each of your classes; see as much as possible in the beginning of your stay; sign up for as many ESN activities as possible; and prioritise exploring the Luberon area instead of the typical touristy cities.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: the French students have WhatsApp groups for their classes. Try to join them for notes.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding out how best to study for the exams, as it is quite different from the exams I was used to.
